key_insight: A frontier LLM can generate, refine, and adapt full shuttling compiler code for trapped-ion architectures, producing competitive results without manual algorithm design.
engineering_relevance: This suggests trapped-ion compiler development for new architectures can move from months of expert effort to days, accelerating quantum hardware-software co-design.
method: Generated full Python shuttling compilers from written specs using Claude Opus 4.7.
Built the system incrementally: linear segmented trap, then junction traps, then general connected trap graphs.
Seeded later compilers with code from earlier versions and benchmarked against hand-crafted state-of-the-art compilers.
evidence_signal: Across a common circuit suite, the LLM-generated compilers reduced shuttling timesteps by up to 76% for linear segmented traps and 39% for junction traps, with strong connectivity-dependent gains in general graphs.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on architecture connectivity, so results may vary substantially for corridor-like layouts versus densely connected traps and should be validated per device.
paper_title: Efficient LLM-Generated Shuttling Compilers for Complex Trapped-Ion Architectures
